newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said five percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, 12 percent in poor, 33 percent fair, 42 percent good and eight percent excellent.

In its report on conditions for the week ended May 4, USDA said 45 percent of the Kansas wheat crop rated very poor to fair versus 45 percent last week. In Texas, 73 percent of the crop was in very poor to fair condition versus 76 percent last week. And in Oklahoma, 67 percent of the wheat rated very poor to fair versus 71 percent last week.
Thirteen percent of the spring wheat crop was planted compared with five percent a week ago and 21 percent in the same period a year ago, USDA said.
USDA said 50 percent of the corn crop was planted versus 18 last week and 40 percent in the same period a year ago.
The department also reported 25 percent of the cotton crop was planted, compared with 31 percent in the same period in 1996 and the five-year average of 37 percent.
Twenty-two percent of the sorghum crop was planted, compared to 25 percent one year ago and the five-year average of 25 percent.
USDA also said 60 percent of the U.S. rice crop was planted verus 56 percent one year ago and the five-year average of 57 percent.
